items.title: refactor: free runtime lines with no behaviour change, and make the dense guard lines readable
items.why: The 1-line headroom blocks every runtime fix; a prototype in scratch frees 26 lines with no behaviour change and showed that 3 of the 5 OPS alternatives called equivalent are not.
items.promise: Free at least 22 runtime lines with no behaviour change, and make the two dense guard lines the shell-doors quality gate named readable. items.title: Probe: does a team-level orchestration gap stay true and quiet on a resumed day?
items.why: Red-team learning for the riskiest item (1180), ranked first by the lead charter; runs before #1172 merges, needs no PR.

In a git archive copy of main (646e4625) under the seat's scratch folder, prototype the two orchestration counts as a throwaway function: open PRs with no shepherd seat running, and gates owed on green heads with no gate seat running. Measure three things. (1) Whether a seat.started row from a session that died without a stop hides the gap, for two liveness rules: seats started today, and seats started in the current session. (2) How many reminders hook.stop gives across two stops when the line carries a count that moves (29 to 28) and when it carries no count. (3) Both counts on today's taoq-ai/wuwei board. The planner records the results with wuwei plan run 1180-probe --reason and passes them to 1180's builder. Out of scope: any change to the repository. Files: scratch only. Runtime budget: 0 lines.
acceptance: Given a git archive copy of main at 646e4625 in a new scratch folder and a ledger with a shepherd seat.started row and no stop, when the prototype computes the shepherd line under each liveness rule, then the probe reports whether the line is hidden under each.

Given the probe's results, when the planner records them with wuwei plan run I-1180-probe --reason, then I-1180's brief names the liveness rule and the line text to build.
items.reason: Measured in a git archive of 646e4625. (1) Rule 'seats started today' (what hook.running does) HIDES the gap when a dead session's shepherd started earlier today and never stopped; rule 'seat.started in the current session_id and not stopped' shows it, and is hidden only by a live current-session seat. Yesterday's dead seats and Codex-only days (no seat rows) are shown by both. Also hook.stop returns None while running()>0, so one dead seat today silences every Stop reminder. (2) Two stops, same session: line with a moving count (29 to 28) gives 2 reminders; same text with no count gives 1. (3) Today's board: 4 open PRs (3 draft), 2 heads owed gates, 0 shepherd/sentinel seat.started today; 9 seats started and 2 stopped today. Rule for 1180: liveness = started in the Stop/status caller's session_id and not stopped; no count in the Stop text (count only in wuwei status); fire when >2 open PRs and no shepherd, or owed gates and no sentinel seat.

items.title: fix(guards): the push door reads each refspec's destination the way git does, so feature:heads/main, :, --all and globs meet it
items.why: Round 3 of PR #1155 (parked at aa63d3b after two fix rounds). The guard's own root ref reader misses forms git resolves to main (security gate: 136 holes in 200). Measured in a git archive copy under git 2.54: one batched rev-parse after for-each-ref leaves 0 holes in 348 generated commands that ran real git (157 moved main; main's door passes 152 of them, the head's 121), 0 in the 5,040 commands of the builder probe's ref classes, and reads 15,000 tag words in 0.2 to 1.2 s.
items.promise: Round 3 of PR #1155. The push door reads each refspec the way git 2.43 does. (1) A destination after the last colon is expanded with git's ref rules: main, heads/main and refs/heads/main name the default branch; a leading + keeps its force refusal. (2) The matching refspec :, --all, --branches (and their prefixes) and a glob whose destination can match the default branch are refused. (3) A source alone goes where git itself sends it: every candidate git's ref rules find in one git for-each-ref, plus the ref one batched `git -c core.warnAmbiguousRefs=false rev-parse --symbolic-full-name --revs-only --end-of-options <words>` resolves each colon-less word to (root refs in any spelling, symlinks, nested names, another worktree's refs, any ref store). The tag keyword, negative refspecs (^x), globs and -- stay out of the batch; -- is asked last as main-worktree/--. Round 2's root ref file reader is removed. (4) When git cannot run or finish either read in 5 s, the door stays shut. (5) Existing refusals (--mirror, explicit main) keep their text. Files: cli/wuwei/guards.py and its vendored copy, tests/test_guards.py, tests/fixtures/routes.json, SECURITY.md, the push door lines in docs/design.md and doors.md, specs/push-refspecs/. items.title: docs(charters): every seat's model and effort come from one table drawn from Anthropic's guidance, which the planner follows and may depart from with a reason

items.promise: Ships in the plugin for every repository running WUWEI. charters/planner.md gains "Model and effort" with the default table, and docs/site/concepts/models.md gives the reasons and sources (Anthropic's model table as cached 2026-10-06 and the Claude Code docs read 2026-10-18: sub-agents, hooks, skills, plugin components). Inputs are signals WUWEI already computes: the item tier, risky and owner paths, contract files, and the change-failure-rate rule that raises a tier. Table: lead Opus 5.5 xhigh; builder Opus 5.5 high at full tier or on trust paths, Opus 5.5 medium at standard, Sonnet 5.5 medium at light; sentinel-security Opus 5.5 high, xhigh at full tier or on trust paths; sentinel-arch Opus 5.5 high; sentinel-quality Opus 5.5 high at full tier or on trust paths, Sonnet 5.5 high elsewhere; sentinel-goal Sonnet 5.5 high; shepherd Sonnet 5.5 medium, Opus 5.5 high for a conflict where both sides changed logic; steward Opus 5.5 high; lookups and searches Haiku 5.5 low. items.why: Bug #1074, which the owner opened on 2026-10-16: the create door refuses gh pr create --draft, which departs from the owner's #1050 ruling and blocks every repository whose CI runs only on PRs.
items.promise: The raise follows the owner's #1050 ruling, which the owner restated in #1074: open as draft, gate at the draft head after CI, then flip to ready. Create door: a draft passes before its gates. That covers gh pr create or gh pr new with --draft or -d, gh api POST repos/<r>/pulls with draft=true (from -f, -F or a --input JSON "draft": true), and MCP create_pull_request with draft true. A non-draft create stays held as today, and its refusal tells the seat to open a draft. Ready door: the flip to ready is held until the gates the diff needs pass at the PR head. That covers gh pr ready (not --undo), gh api POST repos/<r>/pulls/<n>/ccr/ready_for_review and MCP update_pull_request with draft false. A reviewer request on a draft PR is held the same way: gh pr edit --add-reviewer, gh api POST .../pulls/<n>/requested_reviewers, and MCP update_pull_request with reviewers. The ready door reads the PR once (gh.pr) and reuses create_door on its head, base and body, so it adds no new gate logic. markPullRequestReadyForReview joins the refused gh api graphql mutations, with a pointer to gh pr ready or the CCR route. update_pull_request joins guards.DOORS, so the fail-closed check (#1095) covers it. Review pings need no code: evidence.review_duty already skips drafts (evidence.py line 86). Charters and docs state the order: charters/_way.md (the gates line and the refusals line), charters/builder.md (push, then open a draft), charters/shepherd.md (Raise 1-3: draft first, ready and reviewers after the gates), docs/design.md (the gates row) and docs/site/concepts/doors.md. It starts after free-lines-2 (2,996 on main 8ea4192, 2,962 after).
